title: the saveslate proof reads its host from the system device's host tool
intention: The saveslate proof reads its host from the system device's host tool: skills/saveslate/proofs/test_a_slate_names_the_claude_that_wrote_it.py:31 read the host from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host and nowhere else, so this component names its box on every OS.
why: Akien, 2026-11-21, relayed by akiendelllinux_cc_orchestrator: "hostname should come from the system device." Folded into outline 6.6.3.7 and 2.3.7.1.5 (branch akiendelllinux/host-door-outline, 97b4ce0b7). Measured 2026-11-21: skills/saveslate/proofs/test_a_slate_names_the_claude_that_wrote_it.py:31 (HOST = os.uname().nodename) spell the host by hand, so a box with no os.uname (Windows) or a nodename the roster does not spell breaks here. Child of spanning ticket a577fd03e307 (one door names the host). Ticket 5ccc7f05c932 (READY c9824d056 on branch akiendelllinux/5ccc-host-door) builds the door, cairn/devices/system_rackmount/tools/host/host.py; this build starts after it lands on main, because the tool does not exist on main before then.
traces_to: Outline 6.6.3.7 (the hostname comes from the system device); outline 2.3.7.1.5 (the system device's host tool is one of the client tools a device publishes, the named exception to 2.3.7; a CC by-line builds, 0.4.1); outline 17.26.1 (a published client tool lives with its device); RULE 1 (the system device's public interface is the tool it publishes); Law 1 (one answer, not N re-derivations of it).
how: Line 31 becomes `HOST = host_name()` from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host. Add one tooth that deletes os.uname, loads the file by importlib.util.spec_from_file_location under a fresh module name, and asserts its HOST; restore os.uname in finally. PROVES gains this ticket's id keyed to that tooth. A proof-only build: set top-level writes_to to the proof. This is the proof of the very skill that crashed on Windows.

clauses.claim: an AST scan of skills/saveslate/proofs/test_a_slate_names_the_claude_that_wrote_it.py finds no call to os.uname, platform.node, platform.uname or socket.gethostname, and every host name those files read comes from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host.host_name

the proof module loads with os.uname deleted from the os module, and its HOST equals cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host.host_name(): a tooth inside it loads a second copy of the file by importlib with os.uname absent and compares

decisions.text: D1 (clause 1): HOST = host_name() from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host; tooth test_this_proof_asks_the_os_no_hostname scans this file's AST for os.uname, platform.node, platform.uname and socket.gethostname (attribute and from-import spellings) and asserts HOST is the tool's answer.

D2 (clause 2): tooth test_this_proof_loads_with_os_uname_gone deletes os.uname (clearing platform._uname_cache before and after), loads a second copy of the file by importlib.util.spec_from_file_location, and compares its HOST to the tool's; os.uname restored in finally. PROVES keys both teeth beside the keys already there.

out: every other component's host sites (siblings under a577fd03e307)
OS-family checks (platform.system, sys.platform, os.name): outline 6.6.3.7 claims the hostname only

measured.how: grep -rnE 'os\.uname\(\)|platform\.node\(\)|socket\.gethostname\(\)|platform\.uname\(\)' over cairn/ skills/ bin/ on branch akiendelllinux/5ccc-host-door (c9824d056)

measured.saw: clause 2 passes against the unbuilt code on Linux: deleting os.uname in-process cannot red it, because platform.node() falls back to socket.gethostname() there, so on this box it is a hollow green that measures nothing
measured.how: the new proof run in this ticket's worktree with the code file put back to HEAD's bytes, bin/cairn test --exec, akiendelllinux (akiendelllinux_cc_0)

builder_notes: BEFORE PROVED: akiendell_cc_0 runs this ticket's proof natively on Windows (os.uname absent there) once it is relaunched, and records that verdict on this ticket; it is clause 2's real measurement (orchestrator, 2026-11-21)
